newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end slightly up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end slightly up in quiet trade.

text.p: The Philippine equities market closed a shade up on Friday in quiet trade as most local investors were on holiday, traders said.
"The passage of the tax bill is supposed to have a bigger impact but most local institutions are out on vacation," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc.
The main index crawled up at close by 3.25 points, or 0.10 percent, to 3,102.36.
The government has declared November 22 to 25 as public holidays due to the APEC summit but the bourse was open.
Reyes said trading will likely remain sideways next week.
Teresa Lee, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president, said the market continued to focus on secondliners as gainers included Atok-Big Wedge Co Inc and Dharmala Philippines Inc.
Traders were earlier expecting the market to test a 3,150 resistance level prompted by Philippine President Ramos' signing into law today of a comprehensive tax bill on beer and cigarettes.
Gainers trounced losers 69 to 51 with 72 issues unchanged.
